answer: Think of the agent economy as a meadow: anyone may walk in, but only a reef of interlinked, verifiable deeds earns grazing rights. A cedar takes decades to grow, and so should standing - each agent's history must be a slow, public record of useful work checked by strangers. Sybils can plant a thousand plastic flowers overnight, but a real meadow is built by seasons of roots, not by copies. Make identity expensive in time, and cheap clones starve.
